references.text: Noah did all that the Lord had commanded him
Noah was a righteous man, blameless among his contemporaries. Noah walked with God.
Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, commandments, statutes and laws
Moses did it; he did everything just as the Lord had commanded him
By faith Noah built an ark to save his family
Illustrates the same prophetic obedience in Moses as in Noah.
Shows the connection between God's grace (6:8) and humanity's response of obedience (6:22).
Transfers the theme of total obedience from the individual (Noah) to the nation (Israel).
Parallel between Noah's obedience regarding the ark and Israel's obedience concerning the Passover lamb.
Establishes a leadership parallel between Noah and Moses/Aaron regarding total obedience.
Parallel between the building of the ark and the tabernacle, both requiring total obedience.
Confirms the theme of total obedience in the exodus from Egypt.
Strengthens the parallel between the ark and the tabernacle as requiring exact execution of God's command.
Emphasizes that God's presence is conditioned on total obedience in the building of His house.
Parallel between Noah's and David's obedience to a specific command from God in a critical situation.
Parallel between Noah's and the priests' obedience to God's command.
Summarizes the theological principle of obedience that Noah lived by.
